hardDay.heading: Feeling dry? Start here.
hardDay.body:
Some days you won't feel powerful. You'll feel empty or numb. That doesn't mean the Spirit has left you. Dry seasons are real.

Keep the ordinary means, even small. Read less if you must, but read. Pray shorter if you must, but pray. Don't isolate. Tell a trusted believer, "I feel empty," and let them pray. Then do one small obedience while joy returns. Read "When You Feel Dry."

If the numbness lasts for weeks, or you've lost interest in almost everything, please also talk with a doctor or counselor. Getting that help is not a lack of faith.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 6
read.body:
Open to Chapter 6, "The Spirit Empowers Action." Read "God Works in You, As You Work" and "How Dependence Looks on a Tuesday." If you can, read "The Fear Behind 'Waiting on the Spirit'" too.

Some of us learned that if we still feel scared, the Spirit hasn't spoken. That sounds humble. It can become a cage. Moses argued. Jeremiah felt too young. Paul came in weakness.

The Tuesday section is practical. A loud inbox, a tired morning, a hard conversation you've postponed, and what dependence actually looks like in the middle of it. Read it and come back.

read.quote: Weakness is not the opposite of the Spirit’s work.
prompts: Where have I waited to feel unafraid before I moved?

pulse.heading: The pulse: power for obedience
pulse.body:
The Spirit empowers obedience. Dependence is not delay.

Chapter 6 reminds us who the Spirit is. He's the Helper Jesus promised. He gives life, forms Christ in us, equips us, and sends us. Pentecost was power for mission, not permission to freeze. They asked, they received, and they acted.

bookRef.section: Who the Spirit Is, and What He Does; Pentecost Was Power for Mission, Not Permission to Freeze

verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever, even the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, for he dwells with you and will be in you.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

prompts: What does Jesus say the Spirit will do in these verses?

nameIt.heading: Name it: specific or vague?
nameIt.body:
The Spirit's presence isn't proven by the absence of fear. So ask honestly whether your waiting is tied to His Word or tied to feeling safe.

Go back to Philippians 2:12-13, the verse from Stop 0. God works in you, and you work. Where do you need both halves this week?

bookRef.section: The Fear Behind "Waiting on the Spirit"; Reflection Questions

prompts: When I say "I'm waiting on the Spirit," is the wait specific and tied to His Word, or vague until I feel safe?
Where do I need both halves of Philippians 2:12-13 this week?
After praying for help, what small obedience have I postponed while calling the pause spiritual?

build.heading: Build it: check the rails
build.body:
How do you know it's the Spirit and not your fear? Chapter 6 gives rails, not vibes:

The Spirit never contradicts the Word. His fruit looks like Christ. His gifts serve others. His leading usually comes with counsel. And He empowers obedience already commanded. You don't need a special feeling to forgive or tell the truth.

Run your step through the rails. Then plan to take it the same day you pray.

bookRef.section: Discernment: Is This the Spirit, or My Fear?

Rails check: does it fit the Word, look like Christ, serve others, hold up to counsel?

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 6:

Ask the Spirit for help with an honest, short prayer. Then take one clear next step the same day: a conversation, repentance, service, or work done as unto the Lord. Note what happened.

Same day is the key. Pray, then move. If the day passes, pray again and set a new date within three days.

bookRef.section: Practice This Week; Ask for Help, Then Take the Step

prompts: I prayed a short, honest prayer for help
I took one clear step the same day
What happened:
Missed it? New date (within three days):
move.cta: Close the app and go take your step

help.heading: Help: a witness-shaped step
help.body:
Much of the Spirit's power in Acts shows up in a praying, speaking, sharing community, not in lone heroes. They prayed, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.

Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week. Ask them to pray with you before your step. Then think of one person you could encourage, serve, or tell about Jesus this week.

verses.text: And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness.

prompts: The answer I'll bring, and who I'll ask to pray with me:

pray.heading: Pray it: Father, I need You this morning
pray.body:
This is dependence on a Tuesday. Short and honest.

Father, I need You for this morning. I'm weak, and Your power is made perfect in weakness.

If there's something I need to confess, show me. I confess ____.

Holy Spirit, help me while I do this: ____. I'm not waiting for every tremble to stop. I'm asking You to go with me. In Jesus' name, amen.

bookRef.section: How Dependence Looks on a Tuesday

verses.text: But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

prompts: Anything to confess (private to you):

review.heading: Review: filled for obedience
review.body:
After your step, mark it: took it, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 6: fleshly hustle is not Spirit-empowered action. Check your posture. Are you pushing on grit, or abiding? We're filled for obedience, not for display.

And if you feel dry, don't invent energy and don't quit. Ask the Lord to search you, keep the ordinary means, and take the next small step.

bookRef.section: Fleshly Hustle Is Not the Same as Spirit-Empowered Action; Filled for Obedience, Not for Display

verses.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts! And see if there be any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting!
